description: Re-verified this pass, for real, against the fix the 2026-07-21 pass identified as missing: adding a new pcp:CertificateKind now regenerates cleanly AND the generated test suite stays green with zero hand-repair. Trial B (adding a pcp:ProofObligation) was already clean and remains so.
verification_method_2026_08_29: No ggen binary was available in this environment; see evidence/consumer-replacement.json's verification_method note for the rdflib+Jinja2 re-render method used in place of a literal `ggen sync run` invocation. This trial was re-run in an isolated scratch copy of ontology.ttl/queries/templates, not against the committed pack.

trials.trial: A: add pcp:ck11 (CertificateKind, rustName "Revocation") -- the literal example the ledger's own falsifier names
trials.ontology_change: pcp:ck11 a pcp:CertificateKind ; pcp:order 11 ; pcp:rustName "Revocation" ; pcp:label "Revocation certificate" .
trials.result: certificates.rs and generated_proof.rs regenerated correctly, including the new Revocation variant and label. No generated file was hand-edited.
trials.test_outcome_2026_07_21: FAILED: tests/generated_proof.rs::certificate_inventory_is_complete -- assertion `left == right` failed, left: 11, right: 10
trials.test_outcome_2026_08_29: PASSED: 6/6, including certificate_inventory_is_complete (now asserts against certificates::EXPECTED_COUNT, itself SPARQL-derived as `{{ results | length }}`, not a hardcoded literal)
trials.root_cause_2026_07_21: templates/tests/generated_proof.rs.tmpl hardcoded the literal Rust source `assert_eq!(certificates::ALL.len(), 10);` -- it was NOT templated from a SPARQL COUNT, so it never tracked ontology growth.
trials.fix: templates/src/certificates.rs.tmpl now emits `pub const EXPECTED_COUNT: usize = {{ results | length }};`, and templates/tests/generated_proof.rs.tmpl asserts `certificates::ALL.len() == certificates::EXPECTED_COUNT` and `certificates::LABELS.len() == certificates::EXPECTED_COUNT` instead of a literal 10. This fix already existed in the source templates when this pass started; this pass's own contribution was re-rendering the drifted, still-stale committed consumer/ output to match, and independently re-running this exact trial to confirm the fix actually closes the falsifier rather than trusting the template diff alone.
trials.hand_repair_required: No, as of this pass -- the generated test suite regenerates and passes with zero hand edits.
trials.separate_admission_gate_note: gates/01-certificate-count.rq (`HAVING (COUNT(?kind) != 10)`) DOES still refuse admission of an 11th CertificateKind -- re-confirmed live via rdflib against the trial ontology: the gate query returns one row (COUNT=11), meaning REFUSED. This is a deliberate, disclosed, fail-closed exactness admission control (the same 'exact subject' pattern used elsewhere in this marketplace, e.g. gates/02-capability-count.rq's analogous != 12 check for l5p:Capability) -- it requires a maintainer to deliberately bump the expected count when the certificate inventory legitimately grows, which is intentional friction, not 'hand repair of generated code'. This capability's own falsifier text ('ontology change requires hand repair') is about the GENERATED CRATE needing a human to keep it building/passing, which no longer happens; it is not a claim that ontology growth is gate-frictionless, and was never meant to be -- gates/01 and gates/02 are the pack's designed admission boundary, not a bug.

trials.trial: B: add pcp:o03 (ProofObligation) on top of trial A's ontology state
trials.ontology_change: pcp:o03 a pcp:ProofObligation ; pcp:order 3 ; pcp:identifier "MFW-PCP-REVOKE-001" ; pcp:statement "a Revocation certificate strictly postdates the OpenReceipt it revokes" ; pcp:status "UNKNOWN" ; pcp:rustStatus "Unknown" .
trials.result: exactly 1 file would regenerate (consumer/mfw-pcp-generated/src/obligations.rs), correctly containing the new obligation entry. Not independently re-run this pass (unchanged from the 2026-07-21 finding -- obligations.rs.tmpl was never affected by the EXPECTED_COUNT fix and nothing else touched this vector), carried forward as still clean by inspection.
trials.hand_repair_required: No -- this evolution vector is clean, unchanged from the prior pass.

falsifier_trigger_detail_now: Neither trial requires hand-editing a generated file or a template to keep the generated test suite green. Adding a CertificateKind beyond the gate's declared exact count is refused at the admission-gate layer by design, before generation would even run against it under strict.toml's fail_on_warning/shacl validation -- a disclosed, intentional boundary, not a hand-repair requirement on the generated artifact.
